claims.text: A cusp-regulated control policy may predict adaptive switching or hysteresis beyond smooth or reinforcement-learning rivals.
Network heterogeneity and criticality may contribute to flexible cognition, but a Griffiths phase and its adaptive advantage remain unconfirmed.
A regulatory controller may contribute to individual differences or development, but this does not by itself establish psychometric g.

candidate_sources.reason: Process Overlap Theory of psychometric g
Fluid intelligence and proximity to a modelled critical boundary
Evidence consistent with slightly subcritical population dynamics
